newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish BBV cuts prime rate, eyeing inflation.
newsitem.headline: Spanish BBV cuts prime rate, eyeing inflation.

text.p: Spanish bank Banco Bilbao Vizcaya (BBV) said on Wednesday it cut its prime lending rate by 25 basis points to 7.75 percent.
In a statement the bank said the new cut is due to favourable expectations for May inflation, which could fall to 1.4 percent according to its research department.
BBV previously cut rates on May 6 to 8.0 percent versus 8.25 percent. Since then the Bank of Spain cut its key rate on May 16 by 25 basis points to 5.25 percent.
BBV added it also cut another lending rate to its clients.
